clue.text: Celebrate launch

definitions.meaning: to celebrate lavishly is to spend freely on a party, the idiom's figurative sense
taken literally, it is shoving a small vessel off from the shore into the water

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for splashing out on a celebration began as the literal act of pushing a rowing boat off the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for spending generously on a celebration, and literally describes launching a small vessel.

clue.text: Having broken a personal record, though on the decline

definitions.meaning: read literally, having gone beyond the best you ever did
deteriorating with age, no longer at one's peak

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means no longer as good as before; Rufus reads 'past' as 'beyond', so the athlete has surpassed a personal best.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having declined from one's peak performance, and literally reads as going beyond it.

clue.text: Refuse to fight

definitions.meaning: a noun here, rubbish or discarded waste

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb 'decline', but it is the noun for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap means both waste material and, informally, a brawl.

clue.text: Taste before consuming popular fruit

parts.note: tang is a sharp taste

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Sampling a well-liked fruit before eating it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' looks as if it belongs with Taste, eating the fruit, but it puts one short piece inside the other to make ERINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small loose-skinned citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Mother's possibly seen going round in the altogether

indicators.note: going round says one piece encircles the other
possibly suggests the word could be arranged in another way

parts.note: ma is mother, with the s from the possessive

explanation.surface: Mum might be spotted wandering about naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the altogether' means naked, but here reads as 'all together'. 'possibly' makes ENSE, and 'going round' wraps that around Mother's.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French for all together as a group, matching the phrase read literally.

clue.text: Doubter disposed to be intrusive

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A sceptic inclined to butt in where not wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' looks like 'inclined', but here means arranged: it rearranges DOUBTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to push oneself or one's ideas forward unwelcomely.

clue.text: Tips to be shared with those waiting

definitions.text: Tips to be shared with those waiting

parts.words: Tips to be shared with those waiting
parts.note: seems to be about advice passed to people in a queue, but describes a restaurant's pooled gratuities divided among waiting staff

explanation.walkthrough: 'those waiting' suggests a queue but means waiters; 'Tips' means gratuities, not advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tronc is a pooled fund of gratuities in a restaurant, split among staff.

clue.text: Ivan's rule: terrible in general

indicators.note: a nod to Ivan the Terrible, and an instruction to scramble the letters

parts.note: the name Ivan with its s

explanation.surface: The reign of Ivan the Terrible was broadly awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges IVANS RULE; the surface recalls the Russian tsar Ivan the Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying to all cases, that is general.

clue.text: Rock singer about to be detected in depravity

indicators.note: something detected in a word is found sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: depravity is wickedness, or sin
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A rock musician is caught out leading a debauched life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock singer' suggests a pop star, but it means a mythical temptress singing from a rock to lure sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend these sea nymphs sat on rocks and sang to draw sailors to shipwreck.

clue.text: Taking drug, turns to crime in spectacular fashion

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for the adjective, as in a rise described that way

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take in, or swallow, another piece, so it sits within them
turns suggests the letters of the two words are turned about into a new order

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Someone on drugs drifts into a life of crime in dramatic style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes METORIC, and 'Taking' has it swallow the drug's letter; the surface is a slide into crime, not a rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteoric rise is dazzling and swift, like a meteor streaking across the sky.

clue.text: Looks forward to having the last word in pickles

indicators.note: having means holding, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: to predict is to look forward and foretell
amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: Someone anticipates having the final say in a jar of preserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickles' means difficult situations, not preserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a pickle is being in a fix, so pickles are awkward predicaments.

clue.text: He pours out music from his lyre in Greek mythology

definitions.text: He pours out music from his lyre in Greek mythology

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A legendary musician lets music flow from his lyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HE POURS; the whole clue also describes the legendary Thracian lyre player.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical bard whose lyre playing charmed beasts, trees and even the gods of the underworld.

clue.text: Uncle Arthur's day off? It isn't apparent

definitions.note: a clause standing for the adjective, describing something not obvious

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a day off is one taken away, so the day's letters leave the name

parts.note: the name Arthur, the 's linking it to its day
Thu is the short form of Thursday

explanation.surface: A relative called Arthur is taking a holiday, though nobody can tell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes THU (Thursday) from ARTHUR, leaving AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear is not evident or obvious, so it is not plain to see.

clue.text: Nun that is upset about the tedium of life

indicators.note: upset and turned about, the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A nun is troubled by the boredom of her existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness and boredom with the routine of living.

clue.text: Her charges are usually small

parts.note: reads like a modest fee, but charges are the young children in a woman's care

explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' suggests fees; here it means the children she looks after.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny employed to look after young children, her charges.

clue.text: Removed without hesitation and made use of

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to excise is to cut out or remove
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Something was taken out promptly and then put to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it carries its old meaning of outside, so one piece wraps around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or power is to use it, to bring it into play.

clue.text: Converted soul comes here to face lions?

indicators.note: converted means changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Christian convert enters the arena to face lions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' rearranges SOUL COMES; the surface recalls Christians thrown to lions in Roman arenas.
explanation.definitionFit: The great amphitheatre in Rome where people were said to be thrown to the lions.

clue.text: Save money for drinks dispenser

parts.note: save in the sense except, as is bar
tender is money offered in payment, as in legal tender

explanation.surface: Putting money aside to pay for a drinks machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' means except here, not keep.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender pours and serves drinks to customers at a bar.

clue.text: US city editor breaks down on junction

indicators.note: breaks down means falls apart, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: a T-junction is where one road meets another

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor collapses at a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks down' rearranges EDITOR into DETROI.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is a city in Michigan, home of the American car industry.

clue.text: Athletes naturally full of beans

definitions.meaning: competitors in races on the track
runner bean plants carry pods of beans as a matter of course

explanation.walkthrough: 'full of beans' reads as lively, apt for athletes, but refers to runner bean plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners are people who race, and also runner bean plants laden with pods.

clue.text: I ring back about the shrub

indicators.note: about says one piece is put around the other
back says the word for a ring is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: Someone says they will phone back about a garden bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses CALL to LLAC, and 'about' wraps it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a garden shrub with fragrant purple or white flower clusters.

clue.text: Ready to accept simple drink

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb

explanation.surface: Someone is willing to take a plain, uncomplicated drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' looks like an adjective describing the drink, but it is a noun: an archaic term for a herb used as medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is a cool fruit drink, originally a Middle Eastern sweetened beverage.

clue.text: Cage bird to stir? Not half!

indicators.note: not half, read literally, means only half is kept, the first part of the bird's name

parts.note: a budgerigar is a small parrot often kept in a cage

explanation.surface: A caged bird is very excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much'; here it means take only half of BUDGERIGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to move or shift slightly, to stir.

clue.text: Remedy found in no way strange

parts.note: taken as written
St is short for street, a way
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A cure is discovered in some unusual manner.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM as 'odd' is British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a medicine, often a quack one, promoted as a cure.

clue.text: Used by a bowman leading Don Quixote's horse

indicators.note: the leading part, the front portion of the horse's name

parts.note: Rosinante is the old nag ridden by Cervantes's knight

explanation.surface: A bowman leads Don Quixote's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowman' suggests an archer, but means a string player, who rubs rosin on the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is the resin rubbed on violin bows to help them grip the strings.

clue.text: Attractive homes and well designed

indicators.note: the letters are designed afresh, rearranged into a new layout

explanation.surface: Houses that are pleasing to the eye and cleverly planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome means good-looking or pleasing in appearance.

clue.text: Strange sense of locality in Germany

indicators.note: strange suggests the word is made odd, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A peculiar feeling of place while abroad in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges SENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: TV sets remained off for the commercials

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are thrown off their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: The televisions stayed switched off while the ads were on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TV SETS REMAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Commercials are television or radio advertisements selling products.
